scope: our compiled Linux bootstrap: legacy AA version/SSL_HANDSHAKE/AUTH envelopes with real local OpenSSL mutual TLS1.2 and same-session handoff to the verified C receiver; one separately labelled synthetic pending-output API control
cases: literal legacy version request, stable peek, no-progress commit, oversize commit and RX gating
normal cold legacy startup and successful transport-completion gate
every transport byte delivered separately during real TLS handshake
TLS record headers/bodies split across multiple SSL_HANDSHAKE messages
AA FIRST/MIDDLE/LAST envelope assembly before feeding real TLS
explicit API-output injection: drain pending output after real TLS success before AUTH
same transport chunk handoff preserves full encrypted frame and SAME TLS context
same transport chunk handoff preserves partial encrypted header and SAME TLS context
same verified TLS context encrypts outbound opaque reply after bootstrap, real peer decrypts it
mismatched response major rejected before TLS begins
mismatched response minor rejected before TLS begins
explicit version mismatch status rejected before TLS begins
unknown nonzero version status rejected before TLS begins
short version response rejected
extra version response byte rejected
CONTROL instead of SPECIFIC flag rejected
wrong outer channel rejected
AUTH arrives before version/TLS rejected
real TLS verification rejects wrong trusted server hostname without AUTH
real TLS verification rejects untrusted server CA without AUTH
whole bootstrap deadline and uint32 wrap, sticky timeout
failed transport completion is terminal and never makes AUTH_READY
hidden application-data TLS record rejected before handing data to TLS
zero-length handshake TLS record rejected before handing data to TLS
oversize TLS record header rejected before handing data to TLS
stale session rejected without consuming current transport
transport EOF before authenticated completion is terminal truncation
serialized stop clears partial transport/TX storage and rejects later input
all cold/active/error TLS contexts freed and shared allocator integrity verified
limitations: Legacy configurable exact version match, defaults1.1; no current Pixel or Google protocol validation
No general protobuf dispatcher, ping, service discovery, channel open or media negotiation
No actual transport; tx_commit correctness relies on serialized caller reporting successful completion
Final-pending-output control is synthetic API output after real TLS success, not a real final TLS flight
Bytewise startup feed and native ABI/performance unmeasured; no bootstrap ASan claim
No USB host/VBUS/AOA, Garmin hardware entropy/time, decoder/display/touch/audio/UI or installation
No async cancellation/IRQ/task quiescence; stop retains caller-owned TLS and cannot prove hardware mute
